title: Esther Whitley: over the Cumberlands in 1775
summary: Esther Whitley (1755–1833) took the Wilderness Road in 1775, an early woman of European descent over the Cumberlands, and settled near Crab Orchard.
bodyMarkdown:
Esther Gill Fullen was born in Augusta County, Virginia, in 1755. She married William Whitley there, and together they raised eight daughters and three sons. In November 1775, still a young wife with small children, she set out with her husband and family along the [Wilderness Road](https://grokipedia.com/page/Wilderness_Road) toward Kentucky.

The route crossed the mountains at Cumberland Gap and then ran north through hard, broken country. It was a narrow trace, not a road in any modern sense. Families walked or rode, drove a few animals, and carried what they could on packhorses. Esther is remembered as the third woman of European descent to cross the Cumberland Mountains into Kentucky, though early tallies like that are hard to confirm.

The Whitleys reached the settlements in a dangerous time. The Revolution had begun, and raids on Kentucky stations grew worse in the years that followed. William Whitley became a militia leader and Indian fighter, and family tradition holds that Esther was a fine shot with a rifle herself. Life at the stations meant planting, cooking, nursing, and keeping children close inside the stockade when danger came.

The family settled near Crab Orchard, in what is now Lincoln County, on an estate called Sportsman's Hill. There they built a brick house that is described as the first in Kentucky, with thick walls built for defense. Beside it ran an oval track where horses raced counterclockwise, the opposite of British racing. William Whitley was killed at the Battle of the Thames in 1813.

Esther outlived him by twenty years. She died at the home of her daughter Ann Harper in Woodford County on November 20, 1833.

## Kentucky today

The house survives as the William Whitley House State Historic Site near Crab Orchard; its story is told in [Sportsman's Hill](/stories/william-whitley-sportsmans-hill/). The map pin is that house.
